analysis.title: GS Armbrust - What Matters Today: Info Tech Long/Short Ratio at the Lows, NVDA Flows and News, Enough Semis Underperformance?, US Economic 2027 Outlook
key_insights: Hedge funds net sold US equities for a 2nd straight week (5 of the last 6), driven by short sales in single stocks, partly offset by short covers and long buys in macro products. 8 of 11 sectors were net sold, and net selling in US Financials was the largest in 8 months.
Info Tech was again the most net sold global and US sector by dollars. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.5, versus a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June, the lowest on GS's record (since 2016).

Fundamental L/S performance estimate rose +1.16% on the week. Gross leverage fell 2.1 pts to 312.1% (74th percentile, 1-year) and net leverage fell 0.4 pts to 71.4% (3rd percentile, 1-year). The overall book L/S ratio rose 0.1% to 1.593 (4th percentile, 1-year).

Global equities were net sold (-0.7 SDs, 1-year) as de-grossing increased, with long sales outpacing short covers. Energy was the most net bought and most risk-on global sector, bought at the fastest pace in 3 months, driven by long buys.

NVDA flows: earlier long liquidation and de-grossing gave way to a more pronounced pickup in new shorts last week. GS's cash desk saw persistent NVDA supply from long-only holders, with money rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech.

Bessent urged NVDA to pursue a 'dramatic' shakeup and look externally for its next CEO, and the FT reported Jensen Huang is discussing a possible return. NVDA reports earnings tomorrow. Armbrust expects the print is unlikely to resolve the debate on future AI commitments and sees the noise continuing as a headwind for the stock.
Rich Privo's framing: reduced AI commitments could hurt equity growth expectations but help credit as balance sheet risk falls, meaning less spending, better credit, weaker equity multiples.

AMD could benefit from uncertainty around Huang's departure as hyperscalers diversify away from Nvidia. AMD launched 6th-generation EPYC CPUs aimed at agentic AI workloads, claiming up to 3.3x better agents-per-watt versus Nvidia's Vera CPU.

Lee Coppersmith: Semis have underperformed the S&P by more than 30 percentage points since June, the sharpest relative drawdown since 2002, though short of the 1990s extremes. GS Research argues this has gone too far, with some stocks discounting close to zero earnings growth in 2028.
CTA positioning in NDX is back near max short levels. Armbrust says it probably doesn't take much positive news to spark a squeeze higher.
GS 2027 US outlook: GDP growth of 2.4% (above consensus), a stable labor market, and core PCE inflation falling to 2.4%.

GS forecasts consumption growth a bit over 2%, business investment growth of 8% (AI drives half of it but adds only modestly to measured GDP because much equipment is imported or undercounted), and another contraction in housing investment on poor affordability.
GS expects the low-fire, low-hire labor market to last another year before AI displacement has a larger impact.
GS forecasts two more 25bp hikes in December 2026 and March 2027 to a peak of 4.25-4.5%, then gradual cuts to 3.25-3.5% starting at the final 2027 meeting in November.

market_movers.rationale: Armbrust sees leadership noise and the AI commitment debate as a headwind. Earnings tomorrow are unlikely to resolve it, and it may be some time before an 'all clear'.
Could benefit as hyperscalers diversify away from Nvidia. The new 6th-generation EPYC launch claims up to 3.3x better agents-per-watt versus Nvidia's Vera CPU.

tension_points.bull_case: GS Research says the >30pt underperformance versus the S&P since June has gone too far. Some stocks discount close to zero 2028 earnings growth, and CTA positioning in NDX near max short could fuel a squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge funds keep net selling Info Tech, with the long/short ratio at a record low. NVDA faces new shorts, long-only supply and leadership noise, which Armbrust sees as a continued headwind.
tension_points.what_invalidates: NVDA's earnings the day after this note are unlikely to resolve the AI commitment debate, so the bear case persists absent an 'all clear'.
